title: Product and chain rules with an unspecified function
stem: Let f be a differentiable function and let h(x) = x²·f(3x). Which expression gives h′(x)?

choices.label: A
choices.rationale: This forgets the inner derivative 3 from the chain rule when differentiating f(3x).

choices.label: B
choices.rationale: Correct: product rule gives 2x·f(3x) + x²·d/dx[f(3x)], and d/dx[f(3x)] = 3f′(3x).

choices.label: C
choices.rationale: This multiplies the derivatives of the two factors instead of using the product rule.

choices.label: D
choices.rationale: The derivative of f must be evaluated at the inner function 3x, not at x.

title: Product and chain rules with an unspecified function (variant 1)
stem: Let f be a differentiable function and let h(x) = (x + 1)·f(x²). Which expression gives h′(x)?

choices.label: A
choices.rationale: This drops the inner derivative 2x when differentiating f(x²).

choices.label: B
choices.rationale: This differentiates only the factor f(x²) and ignores the product rule.

choices.label: C
choices.rationale: Correct: product rule gives 1·f(x²) + (x + 1)·2x·f′(x²).

choices.label: D
choices.rationale: F′ must be evaluated at the inner function x², not at x.

title: Product and chain rules with an unspecified function (variant 2)
stem: Let f be a differentiable function and let h(x) = f(eˣ)/x for x > 0. Which expression gives h′(x)?

choices.label: A
choices.rationale: This omits the factor eˣ from the chain rule applied to f(eˣ).

choices.label: B
choices.rationale: Correct: quotient rule: [x·d/dx f(eˣ) − f(eˣ)·1]/x², with d/dx f(eˣ) = eˣ·f′(eˣ).

choices.label: C
choices.rationale: This has a sign error in the numerator of the quotient rule.

choices.label: D
choices.rationale: The quotient rule divides by the square of the denominator, x², not by x.

title: Product and chain rules with an unspecified function (variant 3)
stem: Let f be a differentiable function and let h(x) = (f(x² + 1))². Which expression gives h′(x)?

choices.label: A
choices.rationale: This omits the derivative of the innermost function x² + 1, which is 2x.

choices.label: B
choices.rationale: Correct: outer square gives 2f(x² + 1), then f′(x² + 1), then the inner derivative 2x: 2·f·f′·2x = 4x·f(x² + 1)·f′(x² + 1).

choices.label: C
choices.rationale: This loses the factor f(x² + 1) that comes from differentiating the square.

choices.label: D
choices.rationale: This loses the factor f′(x² + 1) that comes from differentiating f.

title: Interpret a composite rate with units
stem: A weather balloon rises so that its altitude after t hours is h(t) kilometers. The air temperature at altitude h is T(h) degrees Celsius. At t = 2, h(2) = 3, h′(2) = 0.5, T(3) = −12 and T′(3) = −6.5. Which statement is correct about the temperature the balloon experiences, T(h(t)), at t = 2?

choices.label: A
choices.text: It is decreasing at 6.5 degrees Celsius per hour.
choices.rationale: This uses T′(3) alone, which is the rate per kilometer of altitude, and ignores how fast the balloon is rising.

choices.label: B
choices.text: It is decreasing at 13 degrees Celsius per hour.
choices.rationale: This divides by h′(2) instead of multiplying.

choices.label: C
choices.text: It is decreasing at 3.25 degrees Celsius per hour.
choices.rationale: Correct: d/dt T(h(t)) = T′(h(2))·h′(2) = (−6.5)(0.5) = −3.25 degrees Celsius per hour.

choices.label: D
choices.text: It is decreasing at 3.25 degrees Celsius per kilometer.
choices.rationale: The units of the composite rate are degrees per hour, since the derivative is with respect to time.

title: Interpret a composite rate with units (variant 1)
stem: The fuel economy of a car is E(v) kilometers per liter when it travels at v kilometers per hour. At t = 1 hour, the car's speed is v(1) = 60 and its speed is increasing at v′(1) = 5 kilometers per hour per hour, and E′(60) = −0.04 kilometers per liter per (kilometer per hour). Which statement is correct about d/dt E(v(t)) at t = 1?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Fuel economy is decreasing at 0.04 kilometers per liter per hour.
choices.rationale: This uses E′(60) alone and ignores that the speed is changing over time.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Fuel economy is decreasing at 0.2 kilometers per liter per hour.
choices.rationale: Correct: E′(60)·v′(1) = (−0.04)(5) = −0.2 kilometers per liter per hour.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Fuel economy is decreasing at 0.008 kilometers per liter per hour.
choices.rationale: This divides E′(60) by v′(1) instead of multiplying them.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Fuel economy is increasing at 0.2 kilometers per liter per hour.
choices.rationale: The product is negative, so fuel economy is decreasing, not increasing.

title: Interpret a composite rate with units (variant 2)
stem: The volume of water in a tank is V(h) liters when the depth is h centimeters, and V′(h) = 12 liters per centimeter at the current depth. The depth after t minutes is h(t), and h′(t) = −0.5 centimeters per minute at that moment. Which statement is correct?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The volume is decreasing at 12 liters per minute.
choices.rationale: This uses V′(h) alone, which is per centimeter of depth and ignores the falling depth.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The volume is decreasing at 6 liters per minute.
choices.rationale: Correct: d/dt V(h(t)) = V′(h)·h′(t) = (12)(−0.5) = −6 liters per minute.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The volume is decreasing at 24 liters per minute.
choices.rationale: This divides 12 by 0.5 instead of multiplying.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The volume is increasing at 6 liters per minute.
choices.rationale: The depth is falling, so the product is negative and the volume is decreasing.

title: Interpret a composite rate with units (variant 3)
stem: The pressure on a diver is P(d) atmospheres at depth d meters, and P′(d) = 0.1 atmospheres per meter at the diver's current depth. The diver is ascending, so the depth d(t) is changing at d′(t) = −3 meters per minute. Which statement is correct about the pressure on the diver?

choices.label: A
choices.text: It is decreasing at 0.3 atmospheres per minute.
choices.rationale: Correct: P′(d)·d′(t) = (0.1)(−3) = −0.3 atmospheres per minute.

choices.label: B
choices.text: It is increasing at 0.1 atmospheres per minute.
choices.rationale: This uses P′(d) alone and ignores the diver's change in depth.

choices.label: C
choices.text: It is increasing at 0.3 atmospheres per minute.
choices.rationale: Ascending reduces depth, so the pressure falls and the rate is negative.

choices.label: D
choices.text: It is decreasing at 0.03 atmospheres per minute.
choices.rationale: This divides instead of multiplying the two rates.

title: Horizontal tangents of an implicit curve
stem: At which points does the graph of x² + xy + y² = 7 have a horizontal tangent line?

choices.label: A
choices.rationale: These are the points where y = 0, which is not the condition for dy/dx = 0.

choices.label: B
choices.rationale: These are the points where x = 0, which is not the condition for dy/dx = 0.

choices.label: C
choices.rationale: These are the points where x + 2y = 0, where the tangent line is vertical rather than horizontal.

choices.label: D
choices.rationale: Correct: dy/dx = −(2x + y)/(x + 2y). A horizontal tangent needs 2x + y = 0, so y = −2x, and then x² − 2x² + 4x² = 3x² = 7, so x = ±√21/3.

title: Horizontal tangents of an implicit curve (variant 1)
stem: At which points does the graph of x² − xy + y² = 3 have a horizontal tangent line?

choices.label: A
choices.rationale: Correct: dy/dx = (y − 2x)/(2y − x). A horizontal tangent needs y = 2x, and then x² − 2x² + 4x² = 3x² = 3, so x = ±1.

choices.label: B
choices.rationale: These are the points where y = 0, which is not the condition for dy/dx = 0.

choices.label: C
choices.rationale: These are the points where x = 0, which is not the condition for dy/dx = 0.

choices.label: D
choices.rationale: These are the points where x = 2y, where the tangent is vertical.

title: Horizontal tangents of an implicit curve (variant 2)
stem: Which statement about the graph of x² + 4y² = 16 is correct?

choices.label: A
choices.text: It has horizontal tangent lines at (±4, 0).
choices.rationale: At (±4, 0) the denominator 4y is 0, so the tangent lines are vertical.

choices.label: B
choices.text: It has horizontal tangent lines at (±2√2, ±√2).
choices.rationale: These points lie on the curve, but dy/dx there is −1/2 or 1/2, not 0.

choices.label: C
choices.text: It has no horizontal tangent line, because dy/dx = −x/(4y) is undefined whenever y = 0.
choices.rationale: Dy/dx = 0 requires only that the numerator be 0, and the denominator being 0 elsewhere does not remove other points.

choices.label: D
choices.text: It has horizontal tangent lines at (0, ±2).
choices.rationale: Correct: dy/dx = −x/(4y) equals 0 when x = 0, and then 4y² = 16 gives y = ±2.

title: Horizontal tangents of an implicit curve (variant 3)
stem: At which points does the graph of y² = x³ − 3x have a horizontal tangent line?

choices.label: A
choices.rationale: At (0, 0) the denominator 2y is 0, so dy/dx is not 0 there.

choices.label: B
choices.rationale: X = 1 gives y² = 1 − 3 = −2, so these points are not on the curve.

choices.label: C
choices.rationale: Correct: 2y·y′ = 3x² − 3, so y′ = (3x² − 3)/(2y) = 0 at x = ±1; y² = x³ − 3x gives y² = 2 at x = −1 but y² = −2 at x = 1, so only x = −1 is on the curve.

choices.label: D
choices.rationale: Only the points with x = −1 lie on the curve, and the points with x = 1 do not.

title: Vertical tangents and undefined slope
stem: For the circle x² + y² = 25, which statement is correct?

choices.label: A
choices.text: dy/dx is undefined at (0, 5) and (0, −5), where the tangent lines are vertical.
choices.rationale: Dy/dx = −x/y at (0, 5) equals 0, so the tangent line there is horizontal.

choices.label: B
choices.text: dy/dx is undefined at (5, 0) and (−5, 0), so the circle has no tangent line at those points.
choices.rationale: An undefined derivative formula at a point on a smooth curve signals a vertical tangent, not the absence of one.

choices.label: C
choices.text: dy/dx = 0 at (5, 0) and (−5, 0), where the tangent lines are horizontal.
choices.rationale: At (5, 0) the denominator y is 0, so the slope is not 0.

choices.label: D
choices.text: dy/dx is undefined at (5, 0) and (−5, 0), where the tangent lines are vertical.
choices.rationale: Correct: dy/dx = −x/y is undefined when y = 0, which gives (±5, 0); there the tangent lines are x = ±5.

title: Vertical tangents and undefined slope (variant 1)
stem: At which points does the graph of x² − 2xy + 2y² = 4 have a vertical tangent line?

choices.label: A
choices.rationale: Correct: dy/dx = (x − y)/(x − 2y). A vertical tangent needs x = 2y, and then 4y² − 4y² + 2y² = 2y² = 4, so y = ±√2 and x = ±2√2.

choices.label: B
choices.rationale: These are the points where x = y, which makes the numerator 0 and the tangent horizontal.

choices.label: C
choices.rationale: The points (±2, 0) lie on the curve, but there x − 2y = ±2 is not 0, so the tangent is not vertical; these come from setting y = 0.

choices.label: D
choices.rationale: The points (0, ±√2) lie on the curve, but there x − 2y is not 0, so the tangent is not vertical; these come from setting x = 0.

title: Vertical tangents and undefined slope (variant 2)
stem: What is an equation of the line tangent to the graph of x² + 4y² = 16 at the point (4, 0)?

choices.label: A
choices.rationale: Y = 0 is a horizontal line, but the slope at (4, 0) is infinite, not 0.

choices.label: B
choices.rationale: This uses a finite slope that does not come from dy/dx at this point.

choices.label: C
choices.rationale: Correct: dy/dx = −x/(4y) is undefined at (4, 0), and the tangent there is the vertical line x = 4.

choices.label: D
choices.text: There is no tangent line, because dy/dx is undefined at (4, 0).
choices.rationale: A curve can have a vertical tangent line where dy/dx is undefined, and the ellipse is smooth at (4, 0).

title: Vertical tangents and undefined slope (variant 3)
stem: A student differentiates x² + y² = 25 to get dy/dx = −x/y and concludes that the circle has no tangent line at (5, 0) because the slope is undefined. Which statement best describes the error?

choices.label: A
choices.text: An undefined slope here means the tangent line is vertical (x = 5), not that no tangent line exists.
choices.rationale: Correct: (5, 0) satisfies 25 = 25, and the tangent there is x = 5.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The derivative is wrong, because dy/dx should be x/y.
choices.rationale: The derivative −x/y is correct for this circle.

choices.label: C
choices.text: A tangent line exists only where dy/dx = 0.
choices.rationale: A tangent line exists wherever the curve is smooth, whether the slope is 0, finite, or infinite.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The point (5, 0) is not on the circle.
choices.rationale: The point (5, 0) satisfies the equation, since 25 + 0 = 25.

title: Tangent line to an inverse function
stem: The function f is differentiable and increasing, with f(2) = 5 and f′(2) = 1/3. Which is an equation of the line tangent to the graph of y = f⁻¹(x) at x = 5?

choices.label: A
choices.rationale: This swaps the coordinates, using the point (2, 5), which lies on f and not on f⁻¹.

choices.label: B
choices.rationale: This uses the slope of f instead of its reciprocal.

choices.label: C
choices.rationale: The slope of the inverse is the reciprocal of f′, not the negative reciprocal.

title: Tangent line to an inverse function (variant 1)
stem: The function f is differentiable and one-to-one, with f(1) = 4 and f′(1) = −2. Which is an equation of the line tangent to the graph of y = f⁻¹(x) at x = 4?

choices.label: B
choices.rationale: This swaps the coordinates and uses the point (1, 4) on f instead of (4, 1) on f⁻¹.

choices.label: C
choices.rationale: This uses the slope of f instead of its reciprocal.

choices.label: D
choices.rationale: This drops the negative sign when taking the reciprocal of −2.

title: Tangent line to an inverse function (variant 2)
stem: Let f(x) = x³ + x, which is one-to-one. Which is an equation of the line tangent to the graph of y = f⁻¹(x) at x = 2?

choices.label: B
choices.rationale: This swaps the coordinates, using (1, 2) on f instead of (2, 1) on f⁻¹.

choices.label: C
choices.rationale: This uses the slope of f instead of its reciprocal.

choices.label: D
choices.rationale: The tangent is at x = 2 on the inverse, so the point is (2, 1), not x = 1.

title: Tangent line to an inverse function (variant 3)
stem: The function f is differentiable and one-to-one, with f(3) = −1 and f′(3) = 5. Which is an equation of the line tangent to the graph of y = f⁻¹(x) at x = −1?

choices.label: A
choices.rationale: This swaps the coordinates and uses the point (3, −1) on f.

choices.label: B
choices.rationale: This uses the slope of f instead of its reciprocal.

choices.label: C
choices.rationale: This has the wrong x value; the point on the inverse has x = −1, so the factor is (x + 1).

title: When an inverse function is not differentiable
stem: The function f(x) = x³ is one-to-one. Which statement about (f⁻¹)′(0) is correct?

choices.label: A
choices.rationale: F(0) = 0 does not make the derivative of the inverse 0; the derivative of the inverse is the reciprocal of f′.

choices.label: B
choices.rationale: The power rule gives (1/3)x^(−2/3), which is undefined at x = 0.

choices.label: C
choices.text: (f⁻¹)′(0) does not exist, because f′(0) = 0 and the formula 1/f′(0) is undefined.
choices.rationale: Correct: (f⁻¹)′(0) = 1/f′(f⁻¹(0)) = 1/f′(0) = 1/0; the graph of x^(1/3) has a vertical tangent at the origin.

choices.label: D
choices.text: (f⁻¹)′(0) = 1, because an inverse function reflects the graph across y = x.
choices.rationale: Reflection across y = x swaps slopes into reciprocals, and the slope of f at 0 is 0, so the reciprocal is not 1.

title: When an inverse function is not differentiable (variant 1)
stem: The function f(x) = (x − 1)³ + 2 is one-to-one. Which statement about (f⁻¹)′(2) is correct?

choices.label: A
choices.rationale: F′ must be evaluated at f⁻¹(2) = 1 and not at 2, and the reciprocal of its value is not 0.

choices.label: B
choices.text: (f⁻¹)′(2) does not exist, because f⁻¹(2) = 1 and f′(1) = 0.
choices.rationale: Correct: f(1) = 2, so f⁻¹(2) = 1; f′(1) = 3(1 − 1)² = 0, so 1/f′(1) is undefined.

choices.label: C
choices.rationale: This evaluates f′ at 2 instead of at f⁻¹(2) = 1.

choices.label: D
choices.rationale: F(1) = 2 identifies the point, but the derivative is a reciprocal of f′(1), which is 0.

title: When an inverse function is not differentiable (variant 2)
stem: The function f(x) = x³ + 3x is one-to-one. Which statement about (f⁻¹)′(0) is correct?

choices.label: A
choices.text: (f⁻¹)′(0) does not exist, because f is a cubic and cubics have a vertical tangent at the origin.
choices.rationale: This version of the cubic has f′(0) = 3, which is not 0, so the inverse is differentiable at 0.

choices.label: B
choices.rationale: F(0) = 0 locates the point, and the derivative is a reciprocal of f′(0).

choices.label: C
choices.rationale: This forgets to take the reciprocal of f′(0).

title: When an inverse function is not differentiable (variant 3)
stem: Let f(x) = sin x on the interval −π/2 ≤ x ≤ π/2, so f is one-to-one. Which statement about (f⁻¹)′(1) is correct?

choices.label: A
choices.rationale: F(π/2) = 1 locates the point, but the derivative of the inverse is the reciprocal of f′(π/2), which is 0.

choices.label: B
choices.rationale: This evaluates f′ at 1 instead of at f⁻¹(1) = π/2.

choices.label: C
choices.text: (f⁻¹)′(1) does not exist, because f⁻¹(1) = π/2 and f′(π/2) = cos(π/2) = 0.
choices.rationale: Correct: f⁻¹(1) = π/2; f′(π/2) = 0, so 1/f′(π/2) is undefined; the arcsine graph has a vertical tangent at x = 1.

choices.label: D
choices.text: (f⁻¹)′(1) = 0, because the sine function has a maximum at x = π/2.
choices.rationale: The maximum of f makes f′(π/2) = 0, but the derivative of the inverse is then undefined, not 0.
